channel.title: The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine (thecenterformichigan.net)

item.title: Are campgrounds a solution to Michigan housing crunch? Some lawmakers think so
item.description: New proposal would allow extended stays of more than half a year at campgrounds in some parts of Michigan. Some are skeptical but one sponsor says it could ‘help solve the housing problem.’

item.title: Bridge Michigan News Quiz, Feb 13: Valentine’s trivia massacre
item.description: Love is in the air. So is the news. Answer these questions to prove your smarts.

item.title: West Michigan faces job losses and uncertainty, as economy takes toll
item.description: Artificial intelligence is leading to job losses. Despite headwinds, business leaders hope to lean into AI and expand tech.

item.title: Purer meth, less pure opioids, more cocaine hit Michigan, testing reveals
item.description: State drug lab results show methamphetamine users now get their stuff from Mexican cartels, not homemade labs. Meanwhile, opioids are being cut with sedatives that make overdose treatments ineffective.

item.title: Lobbyists spent record amount on free meals for Michigan lawmakers in 2025
item.description: Lawmakers and other officials received close to $500,000 in lobbyist-paid food and drink in 2025. Much of the spending isn’t currently visible to the public.

item.title: Mott College trustees to meet about complaint that president is ‘proselytizing’
item.description: Complaints about President Shaunda Richardson-Snell reached Americans United for Separation of Church and State, which sent a letter to the college asking it to stop.

item.title: Michigan tribal boarding school report sought apology. Instead, it was shelved
item.description: Bridge obtained a copy of the 300-page report into treatment at Michigan’s tribal boarding schools that was squelched by state officials. Among other recommendations, authors sought an apology and money to teach what was lost.

item.title: Michigan tribal school survivors recount ‘hell on Earth,’ rapes, beatings
item.description: Bridge has obtained a tribal boarding school study the state put on a shelf. The $1.1 million report recounts horrific tales of abuse at schools intended to assimilate native children.

item.title: Michigan wants schools ready for cardiac emergencies, fails to provide funds
item.description: A recent Michigan law requires schools to better prepare for cardiac emergencies. But without money from the state, some schools lack resources to put those measures in place.

item.title: Michigan gives parolees IDs in bid to keep them from returning to prison
item.description: The Michigan Department of Corrections has provided 30,000 inmates with state IDs and other vital documents before release to ease reentry and reduce recidivism. But exonerees, who are often released on short notice, may not have the same opportunity to secure those documents.
